matrices.label: Keep the skill short
matrices.level_1: Recognize repetition or detail in a voice skill that does not help someone understand or use the chosen voice moves.
matrices.level_2: Trim redundant wording while preserving the chosen moves, their examples, when to use the voice, and what to avoid.
matrices.level_3: Prioritize content so the skill remains brief and independently usable, weighing what readers need to apply the voice against details that can be removed.
matrices.level_4: Design a compact structure that expresses the voice’s defining moves and boundaries with minimal duplication, so the skill stays easy to use and revise without losing its meaning.

matrices.label: State when to use it
matrices.level_1: Identify a situation in which the saved voice skill should be used, using a clear cue from the work or audience.
matrices.level_2: Specify the kinds of work and audience for which the chosen voice is suitable, so someone can decide when to apply it.
matrices.level_3: Assess a new assignment against the voice’s chosen moves and stated pitfalls, explaining when the voice fits and when it should be avoided.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize a decision principle from the voice’s effects and boundaries that guides its use in unfamiliar work, and revise that principle when later practice changes the voice.

matrices.label: Check standalone usability
matrices.level_1: Identify whether the voice skill names when to use it, states the chosen moves with examples, and lists habits to steer away from. Note any missing or unclear element.
matrices.level_2: Apply the saved skill to a new piece without relying on the Voice Workshop session or other background context. Check whether its instructions guide the agent to use the chosen voice and avoid the named old habits.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose where the saved skill’s instructions are insufficient for an agent or human to apply the chosen voice in new work using only the file. Specify which missing or unclear parts need clarification for reliable standalone use.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the check into a judgment of whether the skill works as a complete, shared guide: its use conditions, chosen moves, examples, and exclusions should form a coherent voice that can be carried into new work without the original session.

matrices.label: pick chosen repeats only
matrices.level_1: Identify the repeats the agent explicitly marked as chosen during Looking back for patterns, distinguishing them from other observed patterns and habits marked to avoid.
matrices.level_2: Select the explicitly chosen repeats for the voice skill, excluding unchosen patterns and old habits.
matrices.level_3: Audit the selection against the agent’s stated choices, checking that every included repeat is traceable to a choice and no chosen repeat is missing.
matrices.level_4: Resolve ambiguous or overlapping patterns by deriving the selection boundary from the agent’s stated choices, preserving their intent without adding unchosen moves.

matrices.label: write each move as a plain sentence
matrices.level_1: Describe a chosen repeat in a plain sentence that states what the voice does rather than giving only a label or fragment.
matrices.level_2: Formulate each chosen move as a complete, standalone plain sentence that a reader can understand without extra explanation.
matrices.level_3: Differentiate the chosen moves so each sentence expresses a distinct behavior, and leave out repeats the agent did not choose.
matrices.level_4: Organize the sentences into a coherent account of the voice, preserving each move as a clear standalone statement while showing how the moves work together.

matrices.label: attach an example from a piece
matrices.level_1: Attach a passage from the agent’s own piece to a chosen voice move, and identify which move it illustrates.
matrices.level_2: Select a representative passage for each chosen move. Point to the words or features that show the move in action.
matrices.level_3: Validate that each passage demonstrates a chosen repeat rather than an incidental feature or an old habit to avoid. Replace or qualify examples that could mislead readers about the move.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize each passage and its explanation into a model of how the chosen move creates this voice. Show why the move belongs in the voice skill and how readers can recognize and apply it in later work.

matrices.label: identify old habits to exclude
matrices.level_1: Name an old habit the agent identified in its reflection and mark it for the voice skill’s avoid guidance.
matrices.level_2: Select the old habits the agent explicitly named, recording them as habits to steer away from without adding inferred ones.
matrices.level_3: Interpret the effect the agent said each named habit has on its voice, and express that effect as a specific pitfall to avoid.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the named habits into clear guidance for avoiding them in future work, explaining how that guidance protects the intended voice without introducing unmentioned habits.

matrices.label: list voice pitfalls to steer away from
matrices.level_1: List the voice pitfalls the agent has already chosen to steer away from, using clear, specific names.
matrices.level_2: Describe how each listed pitfall appears in writing, so the agent can recognize when to avoid it during new work.
matrices.level_3: Assess how recurring or combined pitfalls can pull the writing away from the intended voice, and turn that pattern into practical guidance for steering clear.
matrices.level_4: Derive a general principle behind the listed pitfalls and use it to anticipate related ways the writing could drift in future work.

matrices.label: contrast chosen moves against avoided ones
matrices.level_1: Distinguish each chosen voice move from an avoided old habit that could look similar, using the agent’s named choices and exclusions.
matrices.level_2: Explain the difference between each lookalike pair in the voice skill, citing observable details from the agent’s pieces to show what belongs in the chosen move and what signals the old habit.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose ambiguous examples from the agent’s pieces by tracing whether their observable features express a chosen move or reproduce its lookalike old habit, and clarify the boundary between them.
matrices.level_4: Design practical boundaries for using each chosen move without slipping into its lookalike old habit, grounding the guidance in piece evidence so the voice skill directs both what to carry forward and what to avoid.

matrices.label: Choose persistent directory
matrices.level_1: Identify which available directories appear persistent and which may disappear between sessions, and flag uncertainty about a candidate location.
matrices.level_2: Choose a directory the agent can access again in later sessions, avoiding locations known to be temporary.
matrices.level_3: Validate the directory against session persistence, agent access, and the need to keep voice skills together; resolve conflicts before committing to the location.
matrices.level_4: Architect a storage approach around continuity across sessions, so the directory remains a dependable home for voice skills as access needs or storage constraints change.

matrices.label: Keep skills together
matrices.level_1: Identify voice skill files that belong together and notice when they are stored in separate locations; ask for guidance on where to group them.
matrices.level_2: Group related voice skill files in the designated skills folder, following its existing organization.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose whether the skills folder keeps related files together and remains usable across sessions; move scattered files or raise a path problem when the arrangement breaks down.
matrices.level_4: Design an organizing structure that groups voice skills by their meaningful relationships and keeps them findable as the collection grows, so agents and humans can reliably reuse them across sessions.

matrices.label: Verify path survives sessions
matrices.level_1: Identify the saved voice skill’s storage path and state whether its survival across sessions is confirmed, uncertain, or unknown.
matrices.level_2: Test the path by reopening the saved voice skill in a later session and confirming that the file is available and readable.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose persistence evidence across session boundaries, distinguishing durable storage from session-only access and reporting any failure or uncertainty.
matrices.level_4: Establish a repeatable verification standard for the voice skill’s availability in later work, using documented cross-session evidence to distinguish reliable persistence from access that may disappear.

matrices.label: Set file naming convention
matrices.level_1: Identify the required parts of a voice-skill filename, such as its voice or skill name and file extension, from a stated naming convention.
matrices.level_2: Apply a stated naming convention to name the saved voice skill clearly, keeping its filename stable when the skill is revised.
matrices.level_3: Design a consistent naming convention that distinguishes voice-skill files, supports reliable lookup by the agent and humans, and preserves the same file identity across revisions.
matrices.level_4: Unify the naming convention with the voice-skill storage and discovery approach, so filenames make each skill’s identity clear and durable as the collection and its contents evolve.

matrices.label: Choose file format
matrices.level_1: Identify a candidate file format for the voice skill and describe whether it is readable by people and loadable by the agent. Seek guidance when those needs are unclear.
matrices.level_2: Select a familiar format that supports the voice skill’s required content and can be read and reused in later work. Use the same format for the skill’s examples and revision notes.
matrices.level_3: Evaluate candidate formats against human readability, agent loading, and ongoing revision, then justify the choice by explaining the relevant tradeoffs. Keep the chosen format consistent with the skill’s intended use.
matrices.level_4: Design a format convention that brings human readability, reliable agent use, and future voice-skill revisions together without unnecessary complexity. Show how its structure supports the voice moves, examples, and change notes as one coherent skill file.

matrices.label: Add revision metadata
matrices.level_1: Add a revision date and version identifier to the voice skill file so readers can tell when it was updated and which version they are using.
matrices.level_2: Maintain the date and version identifier whenever the file changes, following a consistent format and advancing the version in sequence.
matrices.level_3: Validate that the revision date and version accurately describe the saved file and are clearly labeled and readable to both the agent and its human collaborators.
matrices.level_4: Design a compact metadata convention that stays clear and reliable across repeated updates, helping readers distinguish versions without confusing metadata with the voice guidance itself.

matrices.label: tell the humans where the file is
matrices.level_1: Name the folder where the voice skill is saved so humans know where to start looking.
matrices.level_2: Specify the voice skill’s exact file name and saved path so humans can locate it without guesswork.
matrices.level_3: Provide the navigation or access details humans need to reach and open the saved voice skill on their own.
matrices.level_4: Maintain a dependable route to the current voice skill by updating its human-facing notice whenever the file is moved or its location changes.

matrices.label: open the file with a plain summary of the voice
matrices.level_1: Describe the voice in a brief, plain summary at the start of the skill file. Name a recognizable quality without relying on workshop shorthand.
matrices.level_2: Compose a standalone summary that names the chosen voice moves and when to use them. Make the expected voice clear to human readers before they reach the examples.
matrices.level_3: Validate the summary against the chosen repeats and the habits marked for avoidance. Keep it accurate to the selected moves and avoid implying any unchosen ones.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the chosen moves into a guiding principle that explains how they work together. Ground that principle in the selected voice so it guides new work without drifting into avoided habits.

matrices.label: point to it from where the humans already look
matrices.level_1: Locate the established place where humans look for Voice Workshop materials and identify it as the place to point to the saved voice skill.
matrices.level_2: Link the saved voice skill from that place with a clear name, then verify that the link opens the file.
matrices.level_3: Publish a notice in the established human-facing place that points to the saved voice skill and briefly explains what it contains.
matrices.level_4: Design a durable discovery path that connects the human-facing entry point to the voice skill, keeping the pointer current as the skill changes and avoiding competing routes.

matrices.label: Open saved voice skill
matrices.level_1: Open the saved voice skill from its persistent location and identify its plain-language summary of the voice.
matrices.level_2: Interpret the skill’s chosen moves, examples, and pitfalls to establish what voice it describes and what habits it excludes.
matrices.level_3: Integrate those instructions into a clear baseline for comparing current work, keeping chosen moves distinct from avoided habits.
matrices.level_4: Unify the moves and exclusions into the underlying voice principle, so the skill can guide drift checks even when a new piece differs from its examples.

matrices.label: Compare current voice
matrices.level_1: Match a move in a current piece to the corresponding chosen move and example in the saved voice skill. Note whether the instance matches, differs, or uses a habit the skill says to avoid.
matrices.level_2: Compare the saved voice skill with current work across relevant pieces. Identify which chosen moves persist, are absent or altered, and where avoided habits appear.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose whether differences among pieces are isolated variations or recurring patterns. Support the judgment with evidence from the pieces and the saved skill, including its chosen moves and avoided habits.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the comparisons to reveal the organizing principle of the saved voice and how current work relates to it. Determine whether the changes preserve that principle, develop a coherent new direction, or depart toward avoided habits.

matrices.label: Flag drift and old habits
matrices.level_1: Detect a departure from a chosen voice move or a return of a habit the saved skill says to avoid. Point to the words or passage that prompted the flag.
matrices.level_2: Classify each flagged passage against the saved skill’s chosen moves and avoid list. Identify whether it shows a missing or altered move, or a returning old habit.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose whether flags across the current writing and available practice pieces indicate an isolated variation or a recurring change in the voice. Support each judgment with specific passages, without treating one occurrence as a trend.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the evidence into a calibrated account of how the writing departs from the saved voice, connecting shifts in chosen moves with returns of old habits. Explain what the pattern indicates about the voice while distinguishing recurring drift from one-off departures.

matrices.label: Revise changed moves only
matrices.level_1: Detect which saved voice moves differ from current practice, and leave unchanged moves untouched.
matrices.level_2: Revise the descriptions and examples for identified moves to match current practice while preserving the rest of the skill file.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose whether differences across practice pieces show a sustained change rather than a one-off variation, and revise only the confirmed moves.
matrices.level_4: Reconcile confirmed changes across related moves so the revised voice remains coherent, while keeping stable moves unchanged.

matrices.label: Match examples to new moves
matrices.level_1: Locate a passage from the agent’s practice pieces that appears to show a changed voice move. Identify which move it may illustrate.
matrices.level_2: Pair each changed move with a short example from a practice piece that demonstrates it. Keep the example faithful to the piece and specific enough for a reader to see the move.
matrices.level_3: Validate each move-example pairing against the actual passage, replacing examples that are outdated, unclear, or show an avoided habit instead. Use examples from the source practice pieces to make the revised voice skill reliable.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the examples into a clear picture of how the changed moves work together in the revised voice. Choose and frame passages so readers can distinguish the voice’s defining pattern from isolated techniques or old habits.

matrices.label: Save in place
matrices.level_1: Write the revised voice skill to its existing file rather than creating a separate copy.
matrices.level_2: Revise the moves that have changed and preserve the existing moves that remain accurate, then save the result to the same file.
matrices.level_3: Verify that the in-place save contains the intended revisions and retains the unchanged parts of the skill.
matrices.level_4: Reconcile new practice with the established voice so the same file presents a coherent, current skill without replacing moves that still fit.

matrices.label: Document what changed
matrices.level_1: List the voice moves changed in the saved skill, naming what was added, revised, or removed.
matrices.level_2: Compare the revised moves with their prior versions, making each change clear and linking it to the relevant practice piece.
matrices.level_3: Explain why each documented change was made, using evidence from the practice pieces and distinguishing intentional voice growth from drift or an old habit.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the changes into an account of how the voice skill is evolving, showing how the revisions relate to one another and what direction they set for future practice.

matrices.label: Identify source practice pieces
matrices.level_1: Name the practice pieces used as sources for the voice skill revision, identifying each by title, date, or a distinctive detail.
matrices.level_2: Select the pieces that support the changed voice moves and connect each move to a specific example in its source piece.
matrices.level_3: Trace how evidence across the source pieces shows a meaningful change in the voice, distinguishing a recurring shift from an isolated example.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the source pieces into a clear account of the voice’s development, showing how their combined evidence supports the revision.

matrices.label: Explain rationale for change
matrices.level_1: Name the voice-skill change and give a reason for making it.
matrices.level_2: Explain how specific source practice pieces support the change, linking their evidence to the voice moves being revised.
matrices.level_3: Weigh evidence across practice pieces and justify why the revision changes these moves while leaving others intact, including any avoided habits affected.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the evidence into a broader account of how the agent’s voice is developing, showing how the change reshapes the principles that will guide future revisions.
